audit_findings.title: Pre-Quinnox earnings are paired with a post-Quinnox balance sheet
audit_findings.magnitude: $283.6m acquisition cash paid; debt increased $269.2m from $1,182.6m to $1,451.8m; first-half net interest expense increased $3.9m year over year
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor omits Quinnox earnings, costs, maintenance investment and acquisition financing interest, while the bridge uses post-closing cash and shares.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 20, 2026, the Company announced it entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Quinnox Inc., an agile, results-driven digital solutions provider, for $290 million in cash.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter and timing mismatch. The acquisition closed in March 2026, before the valuation date, yet the DCF still capitalizes FY2025 owner earnings while using the June 2026 balance sheet. The net direction cannot be established because Quinnox earnings increase value while integration costs, maintenance investment and financing interest reduce it. The amounts involved are large relative to the $175.3m anchor and can reasonably change the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild owner earnings through June 2026 or on a post-closing annualized basis, separately identifying Quinnox operating contribution, maintenance investment, integration costs and actual financing interest; rerun with cash, shares and debt from the same date.

audit_findings.title: Serial acquisitions may represent omitted economic capital expenditure
audit_findings.magnitude: $304.1m 2025 acquisition cash outflow, equal to 173.5% of the $175.3m anchor; maintenance-like portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring acquisition spending required to preserve capabilities, customers or earnings belongs in owner-earnings maintenance investment rather than being excluded while acquired-intangible amortization is added back.
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash used in investing activities in 2025 was $343.9 million, comprised of $304.1 million used to acquire TopBloc (see Note 6. Acquisition in Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data ) and $39.8 million used for capital expenditures.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved economic-classification possibility, not a demonstrated calculation error. Nevertheless, six acquisitions in five years and a single-year acquisition outlay exceeding the anchor make even a modest maintenance-like portion reasonably capable of materially reducing value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $175.3m anchor to net income and its $64.8m intangible-amortization treatment, then classify historical acquisition spending between maintenance, replacement and discretionary growth using acquired revenue retention, capability replacement and organic-growth evidence; rerun for the supportable maintenance portion.

audit_findings.title: The 2028 refinancing could raise recurring interest already required inside equity owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $550.0m notes at 4.625%, producing $25.4m annual pre-tax coupon interest; refinancing-rate change unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level owner-earnings DCF, higher refinancing interest reduces future after-tax owner earnings rather than entering as a debt-principal deduction in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has $ 550.0 million of unsecured senior notes, due in 2028, which bear interest at 4.625 percent payable semiannually in arrears on May 15 and November 15.
audit_findings.explanation: The notes and their 2028 maturity are filed facts, but a higher future coupon is not presently established. The July 2026 revolver amendment also changes the financing context. This is therefore a forward-looking sensitivity to monitor, not a demonstrated current error.
audit_findings.action: Before the 2028 maturity, stress after-tax interest across plausible refinancing coupons for the $550.0m notes and incorporate the actual post-Quinnox debt mix, amortization schedule and July 2026 credit-facility terms.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may include required operating liquidity
audit_findings.magnitude: $152.9m, or $3.53 per share; removing all cash would reduce bear value to $36.44 and the 30%-MOS buy threshold to about $37.67, both above the $32.55 price
audit_findings.mechanism: Required operating cash must be excluded from the equity bridge because it supports forecast operations and cannot also be distributed to shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: We believe that our cash and cash equivalents on hand, expected operating cash flows, and availability under our revolving credit facility will be sufficient to fulfill our obligations, working capital requirements, capital expenditures, and anticipated acquisitions (see Note 17. Subsequent Events in Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data ) for the next 12 months and beyond.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing does not establish how much cash is surplus, so the full add-back is not proven correct. However, even the conservative upper-bound correction of removing all $152.9m would not reverse the valuation conclusion: the adjusted bear value remains $3.89 per share above market and the adjusted buy threshold remains $5.12 above market.
audit_findings.action: Determine normalized minimum operating cash after Quinnox, exclude restricted or customer-related balances, and replace the full add-back with demonstrably excess cash; no conclusion-changing rerun is required unless other open findings also reduce value.

audit_findings.title: A new outsourcing commitment may not be fully reflected in the FY2025 run rate
audit_findings.mechanism: The net annual outsourcing cost, after displaced payroll and other internal costs, changes post-2025 operating expenses and therefore owner earnings and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: In the fourth quarter of 2025, the Company entered into a multi-year contract for outsourcing services and the total non-cancelable future purchase obligations related to this contract are reflected in the table above.
audit_findings.explanation: The late-2025 contract creates a credible run-rate mismatch, but the filing only reports $217.2m of aggregate purchase obligations covering outsourcing, job boards, software and subscriptions. It does not disclose the outsourcing portion, annual cadence or offsetting savings, so neither direction nor materiality can be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the outsourcing contract payment schedule and implementation date, isolate its share of purchase obligations, identify displaced internal costs and transition charges, and rerun owner earnings using the net recurring annual effect.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor contains potentially nonrecurring transaction and restructuring charges
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.5m pre-tax, equal to 15.1% of the $175.3m anchor, including $5.2m of workforce-optimization charges
audit_findings.mechanism: Any genuinely nonrecurring cash charge retained in FY2025 depresses the owner-earnings anchor and all forecast cash flows derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: SG&A expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025 included $26.5 million in acquisition, integration, and strategic planning expenses, inclusive of $5.2 million in charges related to strategic workforce optimization initiatives.
audit_findings.explanation: The disclosed amount is potentially significant, but nonrecurrence is not established. The company follows an ongoing acquisition strategy and reported another $22.6m of acquisition, integration and strategic-planning expense in the first half of 2026, indicating that at least part of this spending may recur. The record does not identify the genuinely one-time portion.
audit_findings.action: Build a multi-year schedule of acquisition, integration, strategic-planning and restructuring charges, determine cash versus noncash treatment and recurrence under the forecast strategy, and rerun only for the portion supported as nonrecurring.
